text.text: Front and back pocket measurements of men’s and women’s jeans from popular brands. Across 80 pairs , the biggest divide is not the back pocket—or the width. It is how far a front pocket reaches.
men’s versus women’s average maximum front-pocket height
Average difference: in maximum front-pocket height.
Men’s front pockets are dramatically taller on average. Back pockets tell another story: the average differences are under one centimetre for both maximum height and maximum width.
Average measurements, on a common scale
In men’s jeans, front pockets average 7.12 cm taller than back pockets. In women’s jeans, they are 0.79 cm shorter .
Match each brand’s two men’s styles with its two women’s styles and the direction never flips: men’s average maximum front-pocket height is higher in every matched brand.
brands have a higher men’s average maximum front-pocket height.
Each point is the mean of two jeans for that brand and gender. Brand labels are trimmed and case-normalized for matching; measurements are not adjusted.
Maximum front height · sorted by gap
The gap persists within all three fits recorded for both genders. Boot-cut has the largest average separation; skinny and straight are nearly tied below it.
Shared-fit comparison only. Slim and regular fits occur only in the men’s sample and are not shown here.
Each small block is one pair. Filled blocks reach at least 20 cm in maximum front-pocket height.
A higher price is not a deeper pocket.
Within each gender, listed price and maximum front-pocket height have a weak negative Pearson correlation in this sample. The two gender clouds remain distinctly separated.
Correlation describes these 80 listings; it does not establish what causes pocket size. Prices are not adjusted for style, date or retailer.
80 pairs shown · hover a point for details
The averages are built from individual jeans. Search the complete sample, filter by gender or fit, and inspect the measurements behind the charts.

Measurements in centimetres · price as listed
Women’s jeans average 14.33 centimetres and men’s jeans average 23.13 centimetres. Pocket heights are proportional.

A descriptive analysis of the supplied file data/measurements.csv : “Front and back pocket measurements of men’s and women’s jeans from popular brands.”
One row per jean: 40 men’s and 40 women’s pairs. After label cleaning, each of 20 brands contributes two styles per gender.
Pocket dimensions are shown in centimetres. Maximum and minimum values are reproduced as supplied; averages are arithmetic means.
Gaps are men minus women. Brand matching trims and lowercases labels. Shared-fit charts exclude men-only slim and regular fits.
This is a descriptive snapshot, not a weighted market estimate. Price correlations are not causal, and listed prices are not normalized.
